::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-dcr-001: DCR Is Not a Reachability Certificate. Mathematical Identity (Adjudicated)."}
## DCR Is Not a Reachability Certificate {#claim-ad-dcr-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-math-identity" data-entity-id="ad-dcr-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for DCR Is Not a Reachability Certificate: Mathematical Identity (Adjudicated). Tier: mathematical_identity.">Mathematical Identity (Adjudicated)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-dcr-001`

**Plain-language statement:** A large DCR may flag a modeled acceleration imbalance worth investigating. It does not prove that a golfer is locked-in or that a future correction is unavailable.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** Within a declared model, DCR compares the magnitudes of modeled drift acceleration and the largest modeled input acceleration in chosen coordinates. DCR alone does not prove or determine finite-horizon reachability, path-correction authority, an impact outcome, or a locked-in golfer state.

**Falsifiers:**

- For the scalar system x_dot = d + u with constant d, fixed horizon T, fixed bound |u(t)| &lt;= U and no state constraints, changing d changes the reachable-interval width 2 U T.
- A scalar DCR value alone uniquely determines a finite-horizon reachable set across admissible systems.

**Critiques:**

- **Responded / High:** [Critique: Dimensional Inconsistency of the Drift-Control Ratio](../critiques/dimensional_inconsistency_dcr.html) (`crit-dimensional-inconsistency-dcr`)
- **Responded / High:** [Critique: Drift-Control Ratio (Formalism Overreach)](../critiques/lie_bracket_formalism_overreach.html) (`crit-lie-bracket-formalism-overreach`)
- **Responded / Medium:** [Critique: Normative Ambiguity of Drift (The &quot;Good Drift&quot; Hypothesis)](../critiques/normative_ambiguity_drift.html) (`crit-normative-ambiguity-drift`)
- **Responded / High:** [Critique: Planar Blindness in DCR and Control Cone Analysis](../critiques/planar_dcr_blindness.html) (`crit-planar-dcr-blindness`)
- **Responded / High:** [Critique: Precision vs. Gross Control (The &quot;locked-in&quot; Fallacy)](../critiques/precision_vs_gross_control.html) (`crit-precision-gross-control`)

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Drift, Control Capacity and Golf-Swing Correction](../articles/drift-control-ratio.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered finite-horizon, three-dimensional golfer-club perturbation studies with declared controls, uncertainty, and impact outcomes.

:::

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-dcr-002: Drift-Control Ratio Trends and Their Dependence on the Chosen Kinetic-Energy Metric. Mathematical Identity (Not Reviewed)."}
## Drift-Control Ratio Trends and Their Dependence on the Chosen Kinetic-Energy Metric {#claim-ad-dcr-002}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-math-identity" data-entity-id="ad-dcr-002" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for Drift-Control Ratio Trends and Their Dependence on the Chosen Kinetic-Energy Metric: Mathematical Identity (Not Reviewed). Tier: mathematical_identity.">Mathematical Identity (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-dcr-002`

**Plain-language statement:** In the declared swing model, the ratio of drift to control often grows late in the downswing, but how much it grows, and whether it crosses a given threshold, depends on which weighting or energy measure is used to compute it. This trend does not show that a real golfer or club loses the ability to correct the swing at that moment.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** Within a declared model, the Drift-Control Ratio (DCR) evaluated across a simulated downswing trajectory can trend toward drift-dominant values (DCR greater than 1) during the late downswing interval under the declared coordinates, input set, and norm. This trend, and its magnitude, are sensitive to the choice of weighting or kinetic-energy metric used to compare drift and input accelerations; changing the metric can change whether and when drift dominance appears. The trend does not establish that path-correction authority is actually lost at that instant for any physical golfer or golf-club system.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared downswing trajectory and admissible input set for which DCR does not vary with the choice of weighting or kinetic-energy metric.
- A single scalar DCR threshold that reproduces the same drift-dominance timing across every declared metric choice for the same trajectory.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered multi-metric sensitivity sweeps across declared downswing trajectories, reporting DCR trends under at least three independent weighting choices.

:::

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-decomp-001: Control-Affine Decomposition Is an Exact Equation-of-Motion Identity. Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)."}
## Control-Affine Decomposition Is an Exact Equation-of-Motion Identity {#claim-ad-decomp-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-decomp-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for Control-Affine Decomposition Is an Exact Equation-of-Motion Identity: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-decomp-001`

**Plain-language statement:** The swing&#x27;s equations of motion can be rearranged into a drift part (what the body does under its own inertia and gravity) and a control part (what applied joint torques add). This split is a bookkeeping identity of the declared equations, not a measurement of effort or an independent discovery about the body.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** For a declared rigid-body or multibody system with generalized coordinates x and admissible generalized forces u, the equation of motion can be written in the control-affine form x_dot = f(x) + G(x) u, where f(x) collects the uncontrolled drift dynamics (inertial, Coriolis, centrifugal, and gravitational terms) and G(x) is the input-mapping matrix for u. This split is an algebraic identity of the declared Newton-Euler or Lagrangian equations, not an independent physical hypothesis, a causal attribution of effort, or a claim about which segment of a human swing drives another.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared rigid-body equation of motion that cannot be rearranged into x_dot = f(x) + G(x) u for any admissible choice of f and G.
- The control-affine split alone determines the physiological source of torque, a coaching cue, or a causal ordering between swing segments.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered multibody simulation studies that compare the declared f(x), G(x) split against an independently derived equation-of-motion model for the same mechanical system.

:::

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-icc-001: Intentional Constraint Collapse Describes a Declared Schedule of Relaxing Modeled Constraints Toward Delivery. Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)."}
## Intentional Constraint Collapse Describes a Declared Schedule of Relaxing Modeled Constraints Toward Delivery {#claim-ad-icc-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-icc-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for Intentional Constraint Collapse Describes a Declared Schedule of Relaxing Modeled Constraints Toward Delivery: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-icc-001`

**Plain-language statement:** In the declared model, constraint collapse means a planned, timed loosening of modeled restrictions, like fixed joint relationships, as the swing nears delivery, which changes what motions the model allows at that point. This describes a scheduled change in the model, not a measurement of what a golfer intends or decides to do.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** In a declared multibody swing model, intentional constraint collapse refers to a specified, time-indexed schedule by which modeled holonomic or control constraints, for example fixed joint relationships or torque limits, are relaxed or removed approaching the declared delivery horizon, producing a corresponding change in the system&#x27;s reachable or admissible motion set under that model. This is a property of the declared constraint schedule and model, not a claim about the neuromuscular intent, timing, or strategy of any human golfer.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared constraint-relaxation schedule for which the modeled reachable or admissible motion set does not change as constraints are relaxed.
- The reported change in admissible motion is not reproducible under independent re-evaluation of the same declared schedule and model.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered sweeps across declared constraint-relaxation schedules, reporting the sensitivity of the resulting admissible motion set to timing choices.

:::

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-impact-001: Finite-Duration Impact-Interval Energy and Momentum Accounting Is Fail-Closed Without Declared Contact Parameters. Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)."}
## Finite-Duration Impact-Interval Energy and Momentum Accounting Is Fail-Closed Without Declared Contact Parameters {#claim-ad-impact-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-impact-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for Finite-Duration Impact-Interval Energy and Momentum Accounting Is Fail-Closed Without Declared Contact Parameters: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-impact-001`

**Plain-language statement:** Over the short time the clubhead and ball are in contact, how momentum and energy change is worked out from the declared contact model, meaning how springy the contact is, how long it lasts, and the force profile. If that contact model is not fully specified, the result is treated as unverified rather than assumed to follow any one simple collision rule.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** For a declared finite impact interval from t0 to t1 with a specified contact force or impulse model, the change in system momentum and kinetic energy over the interval is determined by the declared contact model and boundary conditions, and is reproducible from those declarations by direct integration or impulse-momentum accounting. In the absence of a fully declared contact model, including coefficient of restitution, contact duration, and force profile, the energy or momentum accounting for the interval is treated as unqualified and does not default to an idealized, for example perfectly elastic or inelastic, assumption.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared contact model and interval for which the computed momentum or energy change does not reproduce under independent re-integration of the same declared force or impulse profile.
- A reported impact outcome that is produced without a fully declared contact model yet is treated as verified rather than unqualified.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered instrumented-impact studies that compare declared contact-model momentum and energy predictions against independently measured launch-monitor or force-plate impact data.

:::

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-pds-001: Proximal-to-Distal Sequencing Is an Energy-Transfer Property of Declared Coriolis and Centripetal Coupling Terms. Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)."}
## Proximal-to-Distal Sequencing Is an Energy-Transfer Property of Declared Coriolis and Centripetal Coupling Terms {#claim-ad-pds-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-pds-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for Proximal-to-Distal Sequencing Is an Energy-Transfer Property of Declared Coriolis and Centripetal Coupling Terms: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-pds-001`

**Plain-language statement:** In the declared chain model, the way segments are coupled through Coriolis and centripetal terms lets kinetic energy move from inner segments toward outer segments as the model is simulated, producing a speed-up ordering along the chain. This describes a property of the declared model and its equations, not a claim that every golfer&#x27;s body moves this way or that this is the only contributor to clubhead speed.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** In a declared multibody chain model, the Coriolis and centripetal terms that couple proximal and distal segment states can transfer kinetic energy between segments along the chain during a simulated motion, producing a proximal-to-distal ordering of peak angular speed consistent with the declared model&#x27;s coupling structure. This is a property of the declared equations of motion and initial or boundary conditions, not a claim that every human swing exhibits this exact ordering or that the transfer is the sole or dominant cause of distal-segment speed.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared chain model and parameter set for which the simulated peak-speed ordering does not follow the proximal-to-distal direction predicted by its Coriolis and centripetal coupling.
- The reported energy-transfer ordering is not reproducible under independent re-integration of the same declared equations and conditions.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered perturbation studies across declared chain topologies and parameters, reporting the stability of the proximal-to-distal ordering.

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-superpos-001: Linear Superposition Does Not Hold for Coupled Multibody Swing Dynamics. Mathematical Identity (Not Reviewed)."}
## Linear Superposition Does Not Hold for Coupled Multibody Swing Dynamics {#claim-ad-superpos-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-math-identity" data-entity-id="ad-superpos-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for Linear Superposition Does Not Hold for Coupled Multibody Swing Dynamics: Mathematical Identity (Not Reviewed). Tier: mathematical_identity.">Mathematical Identity (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-superpos-001`

**Plain-language statement:** Because the swing&#x27;s parts are coupled and the equations are nonlinear, adding up the separate effects of two inputs does not generally give the same result as applying both together in the declared model. A reproducible example trajectory shows this breakdown directly. This does not say which specific mechanical coupling caused a particular mismatch.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** For a declared coupled multibody swing model with configuration-dependent mass, Coriolis, and centrifugal terms, the response to a sum of two generalized-force inputs is not, in general, equal to the sum of the responses to each input applied separately; an explicit counterexample trajectory exhibiting this nonadditivity is reproducible from the declared equations. This failure of superposition is a structural property of the nonlinear coupled dynamics and does not by itself identify which physical coupling mechanism is responsible for a given discrepancy.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared coupled multibody model for which the summed response to two inputs equals the sum of the separate responses to within numerical tolerance for all tested input pairs.
- The reported nonadditivity vanishes under independent re-integration of the same declared equations and initial conditions.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered input-pair sweeps across declared multibody trajectories, reporting the distribution of superposition-error magnitudes.

:::

## Tangent-Space Contraction Describes Local Linearized Sensitivity Along a Declared Nominal Trajectory {#claim-ad-tsc-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-tsc-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for Tangent-Space Contraction Describes Local Linearized Sensitivity Along a Declared Nominal Trajectory: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-tsc-001`

**Plain-language statement:** Near the declared idealized downswing path, small deviations from that path can shrink over certain stretches, according to the model&#x27;s local linear approximation. This only describes behavior close to one declared path and does not show that the full nonlinear swing is stable everywhere or that a real golfer&#x27;s swing resists all disturbances.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** For a declared nominal downswing trajectory and its linearized, tangent-space dynamics, the evolution of small declared perturbations can exhibit contraction, decreasing perturbation magnitude, over specified sub-intervals, as determined by the eigenstructure or singular values of the declared linearization. This is a local, linearization-dependent property evaluated along one declared nominal trajectory; it does not establish global stability of the nonlinear system or robustness of any specific golfer&#x27;s swing to arbitrary perturbations.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared nominal trajectory and linearization for which the reported contraction over a stated sub-interval does not reproduce under independent recomputation of the same eigenstructure or singular values.
- A declared perturbation within the stated small-perturbation regime that grows where contraction was reported, under the same linearization and norm.

**Critiques:**

## The Wrist Universal-Joint Model Transmits Torque Through Two Declared Rotational Degrees of Freedom {#claim-ad-wuj-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-wuj-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for The Wrist Universal-Joint Model Transmits Torque Through Two Declared Rotational Degrees of Freedom: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-wuj-001`

**Plain-language statement:** The model treats the wrist as a joint with two independent rotation directions, similar to a mechanical two-axis joint, and how torque passes through each direction depends on the current joint angles in the declared model. This is a simplified mechanical model, not a full account of the wrist&#x27;s ligaments, tendons, or soft tissue.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** In a declared universal-joint representation of the wrist, applied torque is transmitted through exactly two declared rotational degrees of freedom, for example flexion-extension and radial-ulnar deviation, and the resulting output torque or motion about each axis depends on the declared joint-angle configuration, consistent with standard universal-joint kinematics. This is a property of the declared idealized joint model, not a complete anatomical account of human wrist ligament, tendon, or soft-tissue mechanics.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared universal-joint configuration for which the computed output torque or motion about either axis does not match standard universal-joint kinematics.
- The transmission relationship changes under independent re-evaluation of the same declared joint-angle configuration.

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-ztcf-001: The Zero-Torque Counterfactual Isolates Passive-Release Dynamics Within a Declared Model. Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)."}
## The Zero-Torque Counterfactual Isolates Passive-Release Dynamics Within a Declared Model {#claim-ad-ztcf-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-ztcf-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for The Zero-Torque Counterfactual Isolates Passive-Release Dynamics Within a Declared Model: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-ztcf-001`

**Plain-language statement:** The pointwise ZTCF family asks what would happen if the muscles stopped pushing right now, inside the model. It shows how much of the motion is carried by momentum, gravity, and linkage geometry alone, within the declared model. It does not show what a golfer&#x27;s muscles were actually doing or prove that one release mechanism exists.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** For a declared multibody swing model, the pointwise Zero-Torque Counterfactual (ZTCF) evaluates the forward dynamics at a given state with all joint torque inputs set to zero, and the stitched ZTCF trajectory re-integrates this zero-torque condition forward from a sequence of such states. Both quantify the passive (inertial, Coriolis, centrifugal, and gravitational) contribution to acceleration or trajectory evolution within the declared model and parameters. ZTCF values do not establish what a human golfer&#x27;s neuromuscular system actually contributed at that instant, nor do they identify a unique physiological release mechanism.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared forward-dynamics model and parameter set for which the zero-torque forward simulation cannot be reproduced from the stated initial conditions.
- The stitched ZTCF trajectory for a fixed model and parameter set is not reproducible across independent re-integrations of the same equations.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered sensitivity studies comparing pointwise and stitched ZTCF trajectories against independently measured passive-release benchmarks under declared controls.

:::

::: {.callout-note .claim-ledger-card role="region" aria-label="Claim ad-zvcf-001: The Zero-Velocity Counterfactual Isolates a Static Gravitational and Postural Baseline Within a Declared Model. Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)."}
## The Zero-Velocity Counterfactual Isolates a Static Gravitational and Postural Baseline Within a Declared Model {#claim-ad-zvcf-001}

<span class="badge evidence-badge badge-qualified-simulation" data-entity-id="ad-zvcf-001" role="status" aria-label="Evidence state for The Zero-Velocity Counterfactual Isolates a Static Gravitational and Postural Baseline Within a Declared Model: Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed). Tier: qualified_simulation.">Qualified Simulation (Not Reviewed)</span>

**Claim ID:** `ad-zvcf-001`

**Plain-language statement:** ZVCF asks what torque would be needed just to hold a position still, with no motion at all. It isolates gravity and posture from momentum and swing-specific forces, within the declared model. It does not measure the torque present during the real, moving swing.

**Formal statement (Bounded):** For a declared multibody model at a fixed configuration, the Zero-Velocity Counterfactual (ZVCF) evaluates the generalized forces or joint torques required to hold that configuration with all generalized velocities set to zero, isolating the gravitational and postural contribution at that configuration from inertial and Coriolis effects. ZVCF values are a property of the declared static configuration and model parameters; they do not establish the torque present during actual motion, nor a causal account of how a golfer reaches that configuration.

**Falsifiers:**

- A declared static configuration and parameter set for which the required holding torque cannot be reproduced from the stated inertial and gravitational model.
- The ZVCF baseline for a fixed configuration changes under re-evaluation of the same declared model and parameters.

**Critiques:**

- No critiques are currently linked to this claim.

**Pages making this claim:**

- [Core Theses Scientific Claim Registry](../articles/core-theses-registry.html)

**Next validation gate:** Run preregistered static-posture studies that compare declared ZVCF holding-torque predictions against independently measured postural force-plate or load-cell baselines.

:::
